sections.html: About 15,400 people live in Moniteau, a rural central Missouri county that sits inside the Jefferson City metro area. California is both seat and biggest city. Households number 5,729 and average 2.45 people, and roughly four in five homes are owner-occupied. Residents value a typical house at $181,900 against a median rent of $735. Builders pulled just 6 permits in 2025, which leaves resale houses as most of what a buyer sees. Clarksburg, Jamestown, Lupus and Tipton are the other towns, with Fortuna and Latham as named communities, and six school districts cover the county.

sections.h2: Which Moniteau County offices handle your tax bill?
sections.html:
Visit the courthouse at 200 E. Main Street in California. The assessor and collector both work weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30, holidays excepted.

  • Assessor, Room 105. Call 573-796-4637 or write assessor@moniteaucountymo.gov. Its job is valuing all taxable real and personal property countywide.
  • Collector, Room 101. Call 573-796-4521. The collector prints the statements, forwards collections to schools and other districts monthly, issues merchant licenses and holds the August sale of delinquent land. Staff work through the noon hour.
  • Recorder, Room 102. The circuit clerk also serves as recorder, at 573-796-2071.

Read each statement closely for the address, listed vehicles and legal description. Payment is possible in person, by phone, through the mail or on the collector's website, with cash, personal check, e-check, money order or credit card.

Houses are reappraised on a two-year cycle. Section 137.115 sets new assessed values on January 1 of each odd-numbered year, and they hold through the following even-numbered year. New construction is handled separately.

Only part of market value is taxed, and the share depends on subclass. Subclass 1 real property is assessed at 19 percent, subclass 2 at 12 percent and subclass 3 at 32 percent. Personal property is assessed at 33 and one third percent, with lower rates for livestock, farm machinery, poultry and a few other items. The assessor can tell you your parcel's class. A manufactured home lived in as a dwelling is taxed at the residential percentage.

An increase of more than fifteen percent on a subclass 1 parcel, new construction aside, requires an on-site physical inspection first. Viewing from the street is not enough. The owner may ask for the interior to be included, with at least thirty days after written notice to ask.

The tax year starts January 1, the valuation date, and payment closes December 31. Personal property lists go to the assessor, and late fees begin if a list comes back after March 1. Anyone living in the county on January 1 should list cars, boats and equipment, and a mobile home on someone else's land goes on the list too. Household goods, inventories, clothing and items of personal use are exempt.

Moniteau County dates to remember
WhenWhat happens
January 1Values are fixed for the year
March 1Personal property list is due, or late fees accrue
Second Monday of JulyLast day to file with the local equalization board
Early NovemberBills are mailed
After December 31Unpaid bills are delinquent
Fourth Monday of AugustDelinquent land can be sold

If November ends and no bill has shown up, call the collector right away. A missing bill does not cancel the tax, the penalty or the interest. A divorcing couple should also know that the collector cannot split a statement after it is issued.

Disputes climb a ladder of three rungs: the assessor, then the county equalization board, then the State Tax Commission. File with the board by the second Monday of July. Once its decision letter is mailed, you have thirty days from the letter's date to go further, a timing rule section 138.430 backs with its "whichever date later occurs" wording.

The commission takes a direct filing, with no board stop, in two situations:

  • Nobody notified the current owner of a new or higher value at least thirty days ahead of the board deadline.
  • A buyer closed less than thirty days after the county mailed the tax statement.

An attorney has to handle any appeal for property held by a corporation, LLC, limited partnership, trust or estate.

Filing a dispute leaves the payment date where it is. To dodge interest, get the whole amount to the collector by December 31 with "paid under protest" on the check and a written note giving your reasons and the value you believe is right. Skip both the protest and the appeal and that year's assessment is final, although next year's can still be challenged.

The Property Tax Credit Claim draws the most questions. The credit goes to certain seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals: as much as $1,100 for owners who occupy their homes, $750 for renters. Your tax or rent paid and your whole household income, taxable or not, set the amount.

A former prisoner of war with a total service-connected disability has a constitutional exemption on the homestead they own and occupy. To claim it, give the assessor proof of residence, a federal letter confirming the disability and either a DD 214 or an archives or VA letter establishing POW status.

Service members away on military orders owe no interest on late payment, though a collection fee may still apply. Confirm current rules with the assessor or collector before you plan around any program.

Before signing a sale contract, get today's payoff from the collector, penalty and interest included. Under section 140.150, land carrying unpaid tax can go to the sale held on the fourth Monday of August. Until that day the owner may pay off the taxes, penalty, interest and costs at the collector's window. A first notice goes by mail to the recorded owner, and when assessed value is above $1,000 a certified second notice follows.

Your closing office should pay off the balance with the collector so nothing is left on the parcel. In a cash sale the payoff simply comes out of your proceeds, with no lender weighing in on an open balance. Gather these before you list: the latest tax statement, the legal description, and the payoff figure from the collector. If the value on the statement looks off, raise it with the assessor before the July board deadline so the number a buyer sees is one you can stand behind. Our Missouri property tax guide explains how appeals work statewide, and the Missouri homestead page covers exemptions. The collector's website carries the current levy sheet for anyone estimating a bill.

faqs.q: Which office sends property tax statements in Moniteau County?
faqs.a: The collector in Room 101 at the California courthouse prints and mails them each November. The assessor in Room 105 supplies the values behind them.

faqs.q: What day do unpaid Moniteau County taxes turn delinquent?
faqs.a: Anything still owed after December 31. The collector then offers the land at the August sale, and the owner may still pay before the sale.

faqs.q: By when must I contest a value?
faqs.a: The county board's filing deadline is the second Monday of July. After the board's letter, you have thirty days to continue to the State Tax Commission.

faqs.q: What share of my house's worth is taxed?
faqs.a: Subclass 1 real property is assessed at 19 percent of true value, subclass 2 at 12 percent and subclass 3 at 32 percent. Your assessor can name the class for your parcel.

faqs.q: Is there a credit for older homeowners?
faqs.a: Seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals may file Missouri's Property Tax Credit Claim, which pays up to $1,100 to homeowners who occupy their house. Income and the tax actually paid set the amount.
